title: UK and EU negotiate landmark reset deal in Brussels
seoTitle: UK and EU negotiate reset deal and youth mobility scheme
dek: British and European negotiators are finalising a reset deal at a summit in Brussels covering food standards, carbon markets, and a youth mobility scheme.
happened: Negotiators from the United Kingdom and the European Union approached a provisional agreement on 19 November ahead of a summit in Brussels on 20 November. The package covers three main areas: a food and drink agreement, the relinking of carbon markets, and a youth mobility scheme. Under the youth mobility arrangement, the UK agreed to allow up to 100,000 EU citizens aged up to 31 to come to Britain each year, with matched numbers for young Britons. Negotiations also addressed higher education fees, with the EU dropping demands for home fee parity for its students in favour of a supplementary agreement to be detailed within six months. Tensions involving France regarding British input into future food laws were resolved, with the UK securing consultation rights rather than voting powers. Prime Minister Andy Burnham travelled to Brussels to finalise the package alongside European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

sides.says: Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that the summit test is whether the deal makes life better for people in Britain, adding: "The test for this summit is simple: does it make life better for people in Britain? That is what I will deliver in Brussels today – cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people."

Nigel Farage condemned the agreement as a betrayal that brings back the debate over whether to rejoin the European Union, stating that it amounted to "betrayal" and noting: "He’s trying to do it incrementally but it’s perfectly clear that this very very soon becomes a debate about do we rejoin or do we stay out?"

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the reset as a win-win arrangement, stating: "A summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security."

next: The agreements are expected to be signed at the Brussels summit on Friday, with the food deal projected to come into force on 1 March 2028 and university fee details to be addressed within six months.
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Union leaders are meeting in Brussels to finalise a reset deal. The agreements cover food and drink trade standards, the relinking of emissions trading systems, and a youth mobility scheme allowing up to 100,000 young Europeans to work in the UK annually. While proponents argue the package will cut household costs and boost growth, critics have denounced the measures as a step towards reversing Brexit.
